summary: Priority promotion caused unexpected refill handoff and soft 429s for background pipeline
description: Customer reports a surge of 429s on their background ingest pipeline that began right after our console-initiated priority promotion for interactive sessions. Initial hypothesis: priority promotion should allocate additional burst credits to the interactive lane only; instead, background pool saw unexpected refill handoff, causing sustained soft-throttling and increased errors on chunked uploads.
impact: Multiple background ingestion workers for Sentinel Maps (dedicated tenant) received 429s for ~45 minutes. Bulk backfills slowed, causing delayed map tile availability. Interactive sessions intermittently experienced higher latency due to scheduler adjustments. Customer-facing SLA risk for dedicated contract.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) In prod-us-east, prepare two logical traffic classes: interactive (low latency) and background (bulk ingest).
2) Simulate steady background upload at 150 req/s (small chunks).
3) From console, promote interactive priority band to +2 weight for 10m (canary rollout).
4) Observe token-bucket reallocation logs and check 429 rate for background.
5) Reproduce observed 429 spike in ~30-60s window post-promotion in our test harness.
observed_behavior: After promotion, refill controller logs show a quick rebalancing event where ~60% of background's burst credits concluded with a delta transfer to an intermediate pool. Background bucket token refill rate dropped by ~40%, generating 429s on previously healthy workers. Some interactive sessions also saw transient latency due to scheduler throttle recalculation.
expected_behavior: Priority promotion should direct extra credits to the interactive lane only, using reserved burst pools or temporary borrow that does not permanently reduce background refill rates. No sustained 429s should occur for background jobs during standard promotional rollouts.

investigation_notes:
- Correlated the event with a console-initiated promotion at 2026-03-10T14:23Z.
- Reproducer run in staging reproduced the delta in token counts when promotion occurred concurrently with autoscaler reconcile.
- Root cause candidate: off-by-one in weight reallocation logic in refill-controller when promotion intersects with temporary pool creation; when the handshake to the intended interactive_pool failed, credits were allocated to a fallback temporary pool that borrowed from background.
- Observed a race between refill-controller and scheduler autoscaler: autoscaler created tmp pools during promotion windows; refill-controller incorrectly computed net delta as "available - reserve" instead of "min(available, transfer_cap)".
- Related PRs: rate-limiter/pull/432 addresses token accounting; scheduler/pull/998 contains improved pool naming to avoid misrouting of transfers.
- Metrics: background 429 rate peaked at 3.2% of requests; token refill throughput reduced by 38% for 45 minutes.
- Escalated to core SRE and runtime team; created INT ticket for patching orchestration flow.

resolution:
Workaround: Rolled back the console priority promotion and enabled an isolated burst pool for background traffic for Sentinel Maps. Client recommendation: stagger background worker retries and add jitter during promotions.
Permanent fix: Patch applied in v1.8.3 to clamp token transfer calculations and avoid fallback handoff to temporary pools when handshake fails. Patch also adds guards to refill-controller to detect concurrent autoscaler events and defer rebalancing.
Follow-ups: Postmortem scheduled (confluence redwood page created), add an observability alert for refill deltas >25% during promotions, and update the console promotion runbook to orchestrate with autoscaler. Ticket will be closed after 72h of clean metrics by Eng/SRE.
